newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares drop 0.85pct on weak large caps.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares drop 0.85pct on weak large caps.

text.p: Greek shares slipped 0.85 percent on Wednesday on weakness in large cap shares and fund managers said the drop was a normal correction to the sharp rise in previous days.

"The market staged a normal correction today after a steep rise of 100 points which bears no important message for the broader market's outlook which remains positive," said Ioannis Vezanis, fund manager at Midland-Ellinovretaniki mutual funds.
Traders said today's downturn was caused by select large caps that came under selling pressure.
"Today's downturn started when Alpha Credit Bank came under fire, in turn affecting the performance of other large cap banks such as ErgoBank and National," said a floor trader.
"Following its recent surge above 7,500 drachmas, OTE succumbed today to selling pressure by large banking portfolios which started in the previous session," said another floor trader.
The mood spilled over to other large caps in the banking and the industrial sector, affecting the benchmark index, he added.
The part-flotation and rights issue of state telecoms OTE which is slated for the coming fortnight bode well for market sentiment.
"OTE's capital increase will act as a booster to the market, attracting new investors," said Vezanis.
The rights issue is not expected to drain the market of its liquidity. Stocks will climb higher after the capital increase is over, he added.
Lower interest rates continue to attract money towards equities.
"There is continuing inflow of funds from investors turned off by easing interest rates as well as by players who cashed in at higher levels," Vezanis said.
May CPI inflation is seen easing to around 5.4 percent from 5.9 percent in April.
Most sectors sub-indices closed lower, with banks shedding 1.24 percent and industrials bucking the trend with a 0.47 percent advance.
The Athens general index gave up 0.85 percent or 14.35 points to 1,670.03 from Tuesday's close of 1,684.38.
Turnover was 34.5 billion drachmas on volume of 6.6 million shares.
